newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves money supply targets unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves money supply targets unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday it was leaving its targets for 1997 and 1998 M3 money supply growth unchanged, in line with market expectations.

The target for 1997 remains at 3-1/2 to 6-1/2 percent growth in the aggregate compared with its average level in the final quarter of 1996. For 1998, the central bank has set an orientation marker for M3 growth of five percent.
The Bundesbank said that, despite problems with M3 in recent years, it continued to see M3 money supply as the main orientation marker for its monetary policy.
The central bank targets M3 in the belief that it offers a good indication of future inflationary trends. However, the figure has often been open to sharp distortions.
"By deciding to maintain its money supply target the Bundesbank is underlining that it continues to regard the money supply M3 as the central guide for monetary policy," it said.
"The development of the money supply has been subject to strong swings in recent years but the long-term fundamental monetary relationships remain sufficiently stable," the central bank added.
It said that it would continue to watch the external value of the mark and developments on financial markets closely when assessing the possible impact of developments on prices.
The mark has fallen sharply against the dollar in recent weeks, while German equity markets have soared to record highs, the DAX rising by around 50 percent this year.
